summary: Vicky terminated the engagement. At 00:00 on Aug 18 she wrote 'Hey guys, I would like to stop this collaboration, can we please count how much money I need to send and disconnect my accounts from Infloww?' — roughly 18 hours after Ollie answered her third chase about the mermaidua second-page problem with the two-word reply 'Yes all solved', and eight days after Derrek said 'give me another hour and ill answer you and update you on all of this' and never came back with the traffic numbers. The whole week was 10 messages. Only three team members appeared at all: Stephski (invoice for Aug 1-14, sent Aug 15 with a changed account number), Ollie (one two-word reply), and Mayson (triage pings). Derrek did not post once in the window and has still not responded to the termination three days later. The only ALTR reply to the churn message was Mayson's 'I'll get you an answer shortly Valeri!' plus Stephski sending a file 51 minutes later — no retention attempt, no call request, no owner escalation. Everything the prior two state files flagged as the churn risk came true: the two-month traffic failure was never evidenced with numbers, the second-page complaint was never substantively answered, Jake's $700 undelivered call went a seventh straight week unmentioned, and the whale list promised Jun 30 was never delivered. The Aug 1-14 (now Aug 1-18) invoice is unpaid and is the last money on the table.

health.rationale: Down from 60. The client formally ended the collaboration on Aug 18 and asked to be disconnected from Infloww. No one at ALTR attempted a save in the 3 days since — Derrek, the owner and the person who owned her #1 complaint, has not posted in this chat since Aug 12. The score is not zero only because she left on cooperative terms, asked ALTR to calculate what she owes rather than disputing it, and the final invoice is still collectable.

Any client who has to ask 'is this complaint solved ?' a third time is already gone.

Change the chase mechanics on complaints: a screenshot from a client should open a ticket with an owner and a due date, and close with a screenshot back. 'Yes all solved' was the last thing ALTR said to Vicky before she quit.
